# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

```text
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Saves the current transition to the history stack.
Algorithm: Push currentTransition onto the history stack and reset currentTransition.
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: currentTransition is empty, history contains previous state.

GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the last move or push transition.
Algorithm: Pop the last transition from history, reverse it, and apply reverse moves to the entities map.
Related Features: history, entities
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: History must not be empty.
Post-condition: Game board state reverted.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Finds the current position of a player based on their ID.
Algorithm: Search the entity map for the Player object matching the ID and return its coordinate.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: id (int)
Output: Position: The current location of the player.
Pre-condition: Player ID must exist.
Post-condition: None

GameState::move
Summary: Updates the position of an entity on the board.
Algorithm: Update the entity map by removing the entity from 'from' and placing it at 'to'.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: from (Position), to (Position)
Output: None
Pre-condition: 'to' position must be valid and empty/traversable.
Post-condition: Entity is relocated.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Checks if the game win condition is met.
Algorithm: Check if every position in the destinations list contains a Box.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Position, Box
Input: None
Output: boolean: True if all targets are covered by boxes.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the entity at a given position.
Algorithm: Return the entity stored at the specified coordinate in the entity map.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: position (Position)
Output: Entity: The entity at the position, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: Position must be within bounds.
Post-condition: None

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Retrieves the current positions of all players on the board.
Algorithm: Scan the entity map for all Player instances and return their coordinates.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: None
Output: List<Position>: Positions of all players.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Saves the current transition to the history stack.
Algorithm: Push currentTransition onto the history stack and reset currentTransition.
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: currentTransition is empty, history contains previous state.

GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the last move or push transition.
Algorithm: Pop the last transition from history, reverse it, and apply reverse moves to the entities map.
Related Features: history, entities
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: History must not be empty.
Post-condition: Game board state reverted.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Finds the current position of a player based on their ID.
Algorithm: Search the entity map for the Player object matching the ID and return its coordinate.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: id (int)
Output: Position: The current location of the player.
Pre-condition: Player ID must exist.
Post-condition: None

GameState::move
Summary: Updates the position of an entity on the board.
Algorithm: Update the entity map by removing the entity from 'from' and placing it at 'to'.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: from (Position), to (Position)
Output: None
Pre-condition: 'to' position must be valid and empty/traversable.
Post-condition: Entity is relocated.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Checks if the game win condition is met.
Algorithm: Check if every position in the destinations list contains a Box.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Position, Box
Input: None
Output: boolean: True if all targets are covered by boxes.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the entity at a given position.
Algorithm: Return the entity stored at the specified coordinate in the entity map.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: position (Position)
Output: Entity: The entity at the position, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: Position must be within bounds.
Post-condition: None

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Retrieves the current positions of all players on the board.
Algorithm: Scan the entity map for all Player instances and return their coordinates.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: None
Output: List<Position>: Positions of all players.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

# Operation Specifications
GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Saves the current transition to the history stack and decrements the undo quota if a move was recorded.
Algorithm: 
  If currentTransition is not empty:
    Push currentTransition onto the history stack.
    If undoQuota > 0, decrement undoQuota.
    Reset currentTransition to a new instance.
Related Features: history, currentTransition, undoQuota
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: currentTransition is reset, history contains the previous transition, undoQuota is updated if applicable.

GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the last move or push transition from the history stack.
Algorithm: 
  If history is not empty:
    Pop the last transition from history.
    Reverse the transition.
    Apply reverse moves to the entities map.
Related Features: history, entities
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: History must not be empty and undoQuota != 0.
Post-condition: Game board state reverted to the previous checkpoint.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Finds the current position of a player based on their ID.
Algorithm: Search the entity map for the Player object matching the ID and return its coordinate.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: id (int)
Output: Position: The current location of the player.
Pre-condition: Player ID must exist.
Post-condition: None

GameState::move
Summary: Updates the position of an entity on the board and tracks the transition.
Algorithm: 
  Identify entity at 'from'.
  Update the entity map by removing the entity from 'from' and placing it at 'to'.
  Record the move (from, to) in currentTransition.
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: from (Position), to (Position)
Output: None
Pre-condition: 'to' position must be valid and empty/traversable.
Post-condition: Entity is relocated and move is registered in currentTransition.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Checks if the game win condition is met.
Algorithm: Check if every position in the destinations list contains a Box.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Position, Box
Input: None
Output: boolean: True if all targets are covered by boxes.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the entity at a given position.
Algorithm: Return the entity stored at the specified coordinate in the entity map.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: position (Position)
Output: Entity: The entity at the position, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: Position must be within bounds.
Post-condition: None

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Retrieves the current positions of all players on the board.
Algorithm: Scan the entity map for all Player instances and return their coordinates.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: None

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Saves the current transition to the history stack and decrements the undo quota if a move was recorded.
Algorithm: 
  If currentTransition is not empty:
    Push currentTransition onto the history stack.
    If undoQuota > 0, decrement undoQuota.
    Reset currentTransition to a new instance.
Related Features: history, currentTransition, undoQuota
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: currentTransition is reset, history contains the previous transition, undoQuota is updated if applicable.

GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the last move or push transition from the history stack.
Algorithm: 
  If history is not empty:
    Pop the last transition from history.
    Reverse the transition.
    Apply reverse moves to the entities map.
Related Features: history, entities
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: History must not be empty and undoQuota != 0.
Post-condition: Game board state reverted to the previous checkpoint.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Finds the current position of a player based on their ID.
Algorithm: Search the entity map for the Player object matching the ID and return its coordinate.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: id (int)
Output: Position: The current location of the player.
Pre-condition: Player ID must exist.
Post-condition: None

GameState::move
Summary: Updates the position of an entity on the board and tracks the transition.
Algorithm: 
  Identify entity at 'from'.
  Update the entity map by removing the entity from 'from' and placing it at 'to'.
  Record the move (from, to) in currentTransition.
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: from (Position), to (Position)
Output: None
Pre-condition: 'to' position must be valid and empty/traversable.
Post-condition: Entity is relocated and move is registered in currentTransition.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Checks if the game win condition is met.
Algorithm: Check if every position in the destinations list contains a Box.
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Position, Box
Input: None
Output: boolean: True if all targets are covered by boxes.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the entity at a given position.
Algorithm: Return the entity stored at the specified coordinate in the entity map.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: position (Position)
Output: Entity: The entity at the position, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: Position must be within bounds.
Post-condition: None

GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Retrieves the current positions of all players on the board.
Algorithm: Scan the entity map for all Player instances and return their coordinates.
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: None
Output: List<Position>: Positions of all players.
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

```text
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).

  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

      // b. Process the action
      ActionResult result = processAction(action);
      
      // c. If failed, print reason
      if (result instanceof Failed) {
        renderer.message(((Failed) result).getReason());
      }
      
      // d. Render updated state
      renderer.render(getState());
    }
  }

```java
                break;

                  {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate players detected in the map");
                  }

                  entityMap.put(position, player);

        }

        gameMap.setMaxHeight(maxHeight);
        gameMap.setUndoLimit(undoLimit);

        gameMap.setMap(entityMap);
        return gameMap;
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```

# Operation Specifications
AbstractSokobanGame::processAction
Summary: Processes a game action (Move, Undo, Exit) and updates the game state.
Algorithm: 
  If action is Exit: set isExitSpecified = true, return Success.
  If action is Move: 
    Check if move is valid (destination is Empty or pushable Box).
    If valid, call GameState.move(), return Success.
    If invalid, return Failed with reason.
  If action is Undo:
    Check GameState.undoQuota. If > 0 or == -1, call GameState.undo(), return Success.
    Else, return Failed.
Related Features: isExitSpecified, state
Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Success, Failed, Move, Undo, Exit, GameState
Input: action (Action object)
Output: ActionResult (Success or Failed)
Pre-condition: Game state must be initialized.
Post-condition: Game state updated based on action, or error returned.

AbstractSokobanGame::shouldStop
Summary: Checks if the game loop should terminate.
Algorithm: return isExitSpecified || state.isWin()
Related Features: isExitSpecified, state
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None
Output: boolean (true if game should stop, false otherwise)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: None

# Requirement
```text
1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).
```
